passage:
In the preschool story corner, Anand's class was talking about secrets. Tarun's hand shot up.
"I tell Mummy everything. Even secrets."
"Even secrets?" Anand asked.
"Yes. Last week a big boy on the van said, don't tell. I told Mummy anyway. She says no grown-up or big kid should ask me to keep a secret from her. I feel safe when I tell."
"What do you do if someone says don't tell?"
"I run and tell Mummy!"
Anand smiled. "Tarun's Mummy taught him something very wise."
After circle, Anand sat with Tarun, heard about the big boy, said it was not Tarun's fault and told the head teacher that day.

qa.q: Who did Tarun tell about the big boy on the van?
How does Tarun feel about telling Mummy his secrets?
qa.a: He feels safe: he says so himself, and he is sure enough to tell her anyway when a big boy asks him not to.

qa.q: What could Anand do next to support the class?
qa.a: Anand could invite every child to name a trusted grown-up they would tell, and repeat that nobody should ask them to keep a secret from those grown-ups. 🙂

qa.q: How might Anand see Tarun's answer?
qa.a: Anand seems pleased, calling it wise, because a child who tells is protected and the other children hear it from a classmate.

grounding: A child knows he can tell his parent anything, including a secret someone asked him to keep, and feels safe.
